_about: What each entity's bodies are made of: the friction and restitution of its .ent, which the original hands the fixture it
builds (planning step 152, WT). DECODED, not guessed. The FRICTION is APPLIED since planning step 263 and the RESTITUTION since step 264 (the engine's
friction solve and its bounce were fixed: friction_applied and restitution_applied below say what they were and what fixed them). What the port's bodies are
built with is the .ent's friction and restitution and the .ent's density as mass, read back by test_mp_timebase against the original's files.
ETHPhysicsSimulator::CreateBody (reference/ethanon/toolkit/Source/src/
engine/Physics/ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:102-109) sets fixtureDef.friction = entity->GetFriction(idx) and
fixtureDef.restitution = entity->GetRestitution(idx) from the <Entity friction=... restitution=...> attributes of the .ent
(ETHEntityProperties.cpp reads them), and sets nothing else a material is made of: no damping (b2BodyDef's linearDamping and
angularDamping are Box2D's 0), so the port's bodies are built with none either (LevelBuilder::MakeRigid).
The solver mixes two surfaces as Box2D does and the engine's PhysicsSystem does: friction by the square root of the product
(CombineFriction), restitution by the larger (CombineRestitution). The port's player has friction 0 of its own (Player::kFriction:
its velocity is set every tick, and a gripping capsule fights its own walk), so a floor's friction touches only the loose bodies:
a crate, a stone, a barrel, a minion. A group whose DECODED friction is 0 (a minion, a gravity agent) applies it even while the
rest is held (apply_decoded_friction): 0 against any surface is 0, so no friction impulse is solved and the engine's solve is
not in the loop.
Every number below was read off the .ent in reference/extracted/assets/entities (the attribute named in each group's _source),
and the _no_emissive and _low_emissive variants of an entity carry the same pair, each checked. An entity this table does not
hold is built with the Godot project's constants (LevelBuilder::kBodyFriction 1, kBodyRestitution 0): these are the entity names
of the 128 levels that have no .ent among the extracted assets - moving_platform, moving_platform_single, enemy_killer, lava, bounce,
no_restitution, collision_128_sqr, single_block, double_block, square_platform_22, rocket_bridge, motor_seesaw - so their pair is
not decoded and stays the old guess (listed in the step's LEFT FOR LATER).
DENSITY is Box2D's mass: b2Body::ResetMassData sums density x area over a body's fixtures, and the group's `density` is the .ent's own
(a static's is 0, and `fixtureDef.density = entity->IsStatic() ? 0 : density`, ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:104). The port's mass is that
density times the AREA of the collider it builds - a box's, a circle's, a hull's, in metres - or `area_m2` where the port's collider is
simpler than the original's: a minion, a knight and the player are two circles of radius 1.3 x 14/2 = 9.1 units (0.182 m, the
compound `body {... radius = 1.3}` of ETHCompoundShape.cpp:69 over the 14 x 36 box), 2 x pi x 0.182^2 = 0.208139 m^2, and the port
builds one circle for a minion and a capsule for the player. So the player weighs 0.104, a barrel 0.432, a crate 0.538, a stone 1.131:
a barrel is 4.15 times the player, where every body weighed 1 before (planning step 152; it is what keeps 2-24's idle player on the
barrel, whose edge he stands on).
An entity with no density here, or that the table does not hold, keeps the engine's mass of 1.
_friction_applied: WHETHER A BODY IS BUILT WITH ITS ENTITY'S FRICTION: TRUE since planning step 263. Every friction below is DECODED and read back from its .ent
(test_mp_timebase), and a body and a surface are built with it, as Box2D does: a crate on a platform is sqrt(0.96 x 0.2) = 0.438, a barrel on a
platform sqrt(0.7 x 0.2) = 0.374, on a block00 sqrt(0.7 x 0.4) = 0.529, a stone on anything is under 0.16.
WHY IT WAS HELD (planning steps 152 to 262), MEASURED. The engine's friction solve walked a RESTING box sideways at a combined friction of about
0.4 to 0.6, and the decoded pairs of the game were in that band: a flat 30 x 30 crate, mass 0.144 or 1, set 1 unit over a flat floor, fell, lay
level and then accelerated along the floor to 5.745 units a second in 30 ticks and kept it for ever, awake; a 29 x 38 barrel 8.78. The same rig at
1.0 against 1.0 slept after 30 ticks, so every body was built at the held 1 below, and a barrel the player pushed dragged where the original's
slides (the owner's report of 2026-11-19, 3-30's small barrel). On level 2-08 (level7a) a scan of the combined friction, every body at one value,
over an idle 420 ticks: 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 slid a few units and stopped, 0.44 and 0.5 crept, 0.6 and above held; in the 128 levels 13 loose bodies
were awake at a constant 5.65 to 6.21 (nine crates) or 8.78 (four barrels) units a second with the decoded frictions.
CAUSE, CONFIRMED BY THE FIX. PhysicsSystem's velocity solve derived the friction tangent AGAIN on every pass from the contact's current relative
velocity and clamped one unsigned accumulated tangent impulse against mu x the accumulated normal impulse as if along a fixed axis, so after an
overshoot (the point solved before it, on a face that is four points) the reversed direction had nothing left to give. The engine now fixes two
tangent axes per contact for the step, each with a signed accumulator (Box2D's own: the engine's ARCHITECTURE.md, Coulomb friction); with it the
rig above lies still at every friction of the scan (0.000 units a second), the decoded pairs included, and test_mp_timebase's tripwire
(TheEngineWalksARestingBoxSidewaysAtTheDecodedFriction) fired as it was written to.
HELD FOR THE RECORD, not used while this is true: held_friction below, and the one group that carried a held_friction of its own
(crate_low_emissive, 3-13's crate, a guess of 0.08 that is gone: it is the decoded 0.96 now, and 3-13 is re-flown).
_held_friction: The Godot project's friction, 1 for a RigidBody2D and a StaticBody2D alike (LevelBuilder::kBodyFriction, kStaticFriction), which the
port's bodies had before planning step 152 and wave 3a's 86 routes were flown on. A body and a surface at 1 against 1 are 1: nothing
slides, nothing creeps (the rig above sleeps after 30 ticks). Not a decoded number: a held one, with the decoded numbers beside it.
_restitution_applied: WHETHER A BODY IS BUILT WITH ITS ENTITY'S RESTITUTION: TRUE since planning step 264. Every restitution below is DECODED and read back from its .ent
(test_mp_timebase), and a body is built with it, as Box2D does: a crate 0.2, a stone 0.15, a lift 0.2, a gravity agent 0.1, the rest 0, and a pair
bounces by the LARGER of the two (CombineRestitution), so a crate bounces on any platform.
WHY IT WAS HELD (planning steps 152 to 263), MEASURED. The engine applied a body's restitution to a SPECULATIVE contact - a pair that is apart but
closing within one step's travel - so a body with a restitution turned round BEFORE it touched, where Box2D turns it round AT the touch (a manifold has
points only when the shapes meet): a stone of 0.15 dropped 100 units onto a floor turned round 5.00 units over it, falling at 567 px/s, and with the
decoded values applied test_mp_demolish's stone broke no wall (it turned round short of the breakable it was thrown at).
FIXED IN THE ENGINE (the same branch as the friction solve): a bouncing pair that will meet inside the step is left alone for the step that closes it, the
next step finds a real overlap and bounces from the velocity the body arrived with (at most 0.15 m deep; not for a body moved after the solve). The rig
above now turns the stone round at the floor (test_mp_timebase, TheEngineBouncesAStoneAtTheTouch).
UNCHANGED ON PURPOSE: the Godot project's 0 (LevelBuilder::kBodyRestitution) is what a body is built with where this table says nothing.

_friction_override: A GUESS (_guess true), not a decoded number: the friction this entity is BUILT with in place of its decoded 0.96 (friction_override, planning step 263; 0.5 until step 264).
crate_low_emissive is the crate of 3-13's slot (level12b; also level2b, level4b and level8c, where it is a plain crate). The level is won by pushing it off its
platform's edge into a 64 px slot between the platform (x 160) and block00_1528 (x 96), where it must lie flat as a bridge (a 58 px crate in 64 px, a 2 px
clearance under wall04). MEASURED, with the recorded play's walk left ending on every tick from 190 to 330 (step 10), on the engine as it is since the friction solve was
fixed, a stack sleeps and a body bounces at the touch (planning step 264): at the decoded 0.96, at 0.45 to 0.9 and at 0.2 to 0.38 and 0.42 no end of the walk wins;
at 0.4 every end from 250 on does (9 of 15). Before step 264's engine it was 0.5 and 0.52 that won, and 0.2: the crate is a CHAOTIC thing of its friction (a neighbour of a
winning value does not win), as it was at the old 0.08, and the value is a guess that this build happens to play. A combined 0.283 against the platform's 0.2, where the
decoded pair is 0.438. The original's Box2D puts the crate flat at 0.96; this engine's contact does not, and the cause is not looked into. To be dropped when the slot's
crate plays at the decoded friction, and to be looked at again by any change of the engine.

_restitution_override: BUILT WITH 0, NOT THE DECODED 0.15 (restitution_override, planning step 264), because the original's own footage says so: the rig clip of 2-29 (test_mp_contact_order,
The2_29StoneRollsAsTheOriginalsDoesAndOnlyBecauseOfTheTable) reads the stone's free roll on the floor at 2.025 units a frame, its landing at f123 and its meeting with the
barrel at f183.5, and the port's stone is at 2.10, f131.1 and f186.0 with no restitution (+3.8, +6.6 and +1.4 percent) and at 1.82, f135.7 and f193.5 with the decoded
0.15 (-10.3, +10.3 and +5.5 percent: out of the clip's +-10 percent bands). The engine's bounce at the touch takes more of a rolling stone's speed than Box2D's does, for a reason
not looked into; the measurement beats the decoded number until it is. A crate's 0.2 and every other entity's decoded restitution are applied.
